edition.label: Sample Edition
edition.disclaimer: Sample edition for illustration. All names, posts, figures and placements are synthetic and do not represent real research or real Sandals or Beaches travelers.

descriptions.volume: How much of the relevant conversation the theme represents.
descriptions.intensity: How strongly people feel when they raise it.
descriptions.momentum: How fast it is growing versus the previous 30 days.
descriptions.relevance: How directly it connects with what the brand offers or promises.

threeLines: Couples are tired of a single picture of romance. They want trips that look like them.
Family holidays are judged by the kids’ joy, and parents are starting to say what they lost along the way.
“What’s actually included?” is still the biggest category barrier, and it is about confidence more than price.

Sandals.text: Couples want a version of romance that reflects their own relationship.
Milestones beyond the honeymoon: renewals, recoveries, years survived together.
Surprises arranged by staff can feel intrusive when couples want privacy.

Beaches.text: Parents describe successful holidays that left little room for each other.
The family planner wants to stop organizing and become a guest.
Kids’ club details are discovered late, after adult plans are already set.

platformNotes.note: Where couples build the picture. Pushback on “template romance” concentrates here (46% of mentions for finding 01).
Where families plan and ask. Groups carry the most detailed questions about inclusions and logistics.
Where proof lives. Unfiltered guest videos are becoming the evidence people trust most before deciding.
Where frustration goes public, mostly around price confidence and “hidden extras.”

culturalWatch.title: Milestones, redefined
culturalWatch.text: Couples celebrate milestones that never had a ritual: a year sober, debts paid off, a hard year survived. They want celebration without the clichés.

culturalWatch.title: The unfiltered review
culturalWatch.text: Raw, unedited guest footage is gaining trust over polished imagery. “Show me the breakfast line” is becoming a test of honesty.

nextSession: Which romantic signals in current Sandals creative might read as “someone else’s honeymoon”?
How could Beaches show adult time without diminishing the family promise?
What proof would make the “all” in all-inclusive feel believable at a glance?

findings.title: Romance that feels like ours
findings.tension: Romance as pictured vs. romance as ours
findings.summary: Couples push back on a single, prescribed image of romance and look for experiences that reflect how they actually are together.
findings.reveals: Romance is personal. Generic romantic signals such as petals, champagne and identical overwater imagery are read as “someone else’s honeymoon.”

findings.title: The family holiday that leaves the adults out
findings.tension: The kids’ joy vs. the couple’s connection
findings.summary: Parents describe holidays that worked beautifully for the kids but left them with almost no time or conversation as a couple.
findings.reveals: A family holiday is judged by the kids’ happiness, while the adults’ need to rest and reconnect goes unspoken until afterwards.

findings.title: What does “all” actually include?
findings.summary: Travelers struggle to compare all-inclusive offers because they cannot tell what is covered and what will cost extra.
findings.reveals: The barrier is confidence in the promise, not the headline price. Guests who stayed often say the value was clearer afterwards than before.

findings.title: The planner wants a holiday too
findings.summary: The person who organizes the family trip says, often with humor, that they want to stop making decisions and simply be a guest.
findings.reveals: For the planner, luxury is the absence of decisions. Relief from organizing may matter as much as the activities themselves.

findings.title: Milestones beyond the honeymoon
findings.summary: Couples plan trips to mark milestones that rarely get a ritual: a delayed honeymoon, a vow renewal after a hard year, sobriety, debts paid off.
findings.reveals: The occasion is the relationship itself. These couples want celebration that feels earned and personal, not staged.

findings.title: Proof over polish
findings.summary: Travelers say they trust unedited guest footage more than polished brand imagery when deciding.
findings.reveals: Believability is becoming part of the aesthetic. Real, imperfect moments may carry more persuasive weight than perfect ones.

sheets.headline: Romance on their terms
evidence: 1,240 mentions this period, up 18% versus the previous 30 days.
17% of Sandals-related conversation; 46% of it on Instagram.
Highest emotional intensity of any finding this month (88/100).
sheets.meaning: Couples are not rejecting romance. They are rejecting a single template of it. When imagery looks interchangeable, they read it as made for someone else.

relevance.who: Engaged couples and long-term couples, especially those who describe themselves against clichés.
relevance.when: Dreaming and early planning, while browsing Instagram and TikTok.
relevance.how: Sandals’ couples-only focus gives it permission to show many kinds of couples and many kinds of romance.

opportunity.statement: Romance on their terms: experiences that reflect each couple’s own way of being together.

alsoConsider.text: Sandals understands couples, not just honeymoons.

agencyQuestions: Which current visuals could read as generic romance?
What does an “ours” moment look like in a 15-second video?
Which real couple behaviors could anchor the story?
unknowns: Whether the pattern differs by market or age group.
How strongly it affects consideration versus engagement.

sheets.headline: Parents get each other back
evidence: 1,105 mentions this period, up 12% versus the previous 30 days.
22% of Beaches-related conversation; strongest on Facebook (38%) and TikTok (30%).
Often expressed with humor, which keeps it from showing up in basic sentiment.
sheets.meaning: Parents measure the holiday by their children’s happiness and rarely complain directly. The missing adult connection appears in jokes and in hindsight.

relevance.who: Parents of children under 12, and the parent who plans the trip.
relevance.when: During planning, and again after the stay in reviews and posts.
relevance.how: Beaches’ family promise can include adult connection without competing with it.

opportunity.statement: The family holiday where parents get each other back.

alsoConsider.text: “Will we actually get any time to ourselves?”
Beaches is designed for the whole family, adults included.

agencyQuestions: How can adult time appear without implying kids are a burden?
Which moments signal that parents can truly relax?
Should kids’ club information appear earlier in the journey?
unknowns: Differences between single-parent and two-parent households.
Whether multigenerational groups share the same need.

sources: Accessible public conversations on Instagram, Facebook, TikTok and X.
method.interpretation: Contextual language analysis with human review of meaning, humor, sarcasm and irony. Classifications can align with segments and variables supplied by the client.
method.boundaries: Conversation is evidence of expressed needs, perceptions, consideration and advocacy. It does not imply verified identities, complete audience coverage, measured ad exposure, causal campaign effects or booking attribution.
